attr.str.desc: Raw power. Swords and spears hit harder with it, and heavy weapons and armor will ask for it.
attr.dex.desc: Quick hands and feet. Daggers, bows, swords and spears hit harder; you attack a little faster and roll more often.
attr.end.desc: A body that holds. +10 health and faster healing for each point; a blow from behind dazes you for less, and a heavy swing slows you for less.
attr.int.desc: A trained mind. +10 mana and faster mana for each point, and staffs hit harder. A staff spends mana on every spell.
attr.per.desc: Eyes that notice. You see farther through the fog, your shots fly farther, and you find weak spots a little more often.
attr.lck.desc: The world leans your way. More critical hits, rare things drop more often, and monsters carry more gold.
attr.cha.desc: People like you. Merchants sell for less and pay more, and quest givers add to the reward. Some people will tell you more.

quest.q_slimes.text: Something seeps out of the north well again. Five of them. Don't drink the water till you're done.
quest.q_wolves.text: Wolves circle the wall, but they never cross it. They know something we forgot. Thin them out.
quest.q_scorpions.text: Since the last Pulse the sand out east moves wrong. So do the scorpions. Four should teach them.
quest.q_swarm.text: There's a tear by the old mill, and it keeps leaking. Fifteen slimes should slow it down.
quest.q_cull.text: The wall holds as long as we pay for it, in stone or in blood. Twenty of anything, please.
quest.q_packleader.text: One pack remembers the wall from before. Break it, and take this ring. Surveyors of the Ring wore them.
quest.q_gate_1.text: Wolves walk right up to the gate while old Hesk stares at the fold. Thin them out.
quest.q_gate_2.text: Hesk's net over the gate catches bats and carters. Kill the bats before it catches anyone else.
quest.q_gate_3.text: Something came out of the fold, and Hesk went after it with a rope. Clear the dark around him.
quest.q_eel_1.text: Slime keeps creeping up from the north well to visit the eel in the font. Stop it at the steps.
quest.q_eel_2.text: Pilgrims walk in to see the eel. Keep the roads safe for people on their knees.
quest.q_eel_3.text: The eel is gone, and the north well is thick with slime again. Just the well. Do not ask why.
quest.q_cellar_1.text: Bats come through a crack in the inn's cellar. Kill them quietly. There is no crack.
quest.q_cellar_2.text: The barrel came back through the crack, and the slime went off toward the mill.
quest.q_cellar_3.text: The innkeeper sells tickets to the crack now. Keep the roads safe for paying customers.
quest.q_cellar_3b.text: A mason is walling up the crack, and everything behind it flew out at the first brick.
elder.say.hamlet.0: The sky dropped a stone and the world cracked. That's all I know. Mind the wells.
elder.say.hamlet.1: Came with a Pulse. Last Pulse it was goats. Be grateful.
elder.say.hamlet.2: We have no wall. We have luck, and luck is cheaper.
elder.say.village.0: The Hand opened, and the Palm holds us. Touch the fence before you sleep.
elder.say.village.1: The priest says the fence is holy. The carpenter says it is pine. Both are right.
elder.say.village.2: A Pulse moved the harvest feast to winter. Nobody minds. Nobody remembers it was ever different.
elder.say.town.0: Stone holds, wood bends, prayer helps the wood. Mostly.
elder.say.town.1: Caravans say the folds moved east this year. Folds don't move. And yet.
elder.say.town.2: Our wall is anchor stone. We paid for every block. Don't scratch it.
elder.say.city.0: Before the Shift there was a Ring. Don't ask me what it was. I only own the receipt.
elder.say.city.1: Our chroniclers disagree about the Shift. Every one of them was there, they say.
elder.say.city.2: After every Pulse the library has a book nobody wrote. We shelve them under Fiction. Mostly.
elder.say.capital.0: We kept records. Then we lost the pages that explain why we kept them.
elder.say.capital.1: The Crown will tell you the truth. Which version would you like?
elder.say.capital.2: The castle stood here before the Shift. Or after. The plaque changes.
note.title: A note
note.close: Click or press any key to put it away
note.crypt.0: Shift 3, night duty. The lights are out. The clock still runs. I do not trust it.
note.crypt.1: Day 12 below. Corridor B is longer than yesterday. I measured. Twice.
note.crypt.2: To whoever finds this: the Ring worked. Tell them it worked. Tell them we are sorry.
note.ice.0: Samples are stable. The people are not. Please send blankets.
note.ice.1: The freezer hums the same note the Ring did. I sleep with earplugs.
note.ice.2: Security keeps asking for my badge. I died last week. It still asks politely.
note.tomb.0: As senior on shift I hereby declare myself king. Nobody objected. Nobody is left.
note.tomb.1: Vault inventory: 3 crates of calibration plates, 1 crown (improvised), 0 hope.
note.tomb.2: The sand outside counts backwards. We stopped asking it the time.
note.cave.0: If you are reading this, the Pulse has not rewritten this note yet. Hurry.
note.cave.1: The passage is shorter on the way back. Always. Don't think about it.
note.cave.2: Bats know where the folds are. Follow the bats. Do not follow the bats.
note.valley.0: Day 1 of the Pocket. Outside, years pass. In here, one lunch. Eat slowly.
note.valley.1: The valley keeps the old sky. Look up before you leave.
note.valley.2: Surveyor's log: ring of cliffs closed, time skewed, tea still hot. Recommend: stay.
intro.note: Three hundred years ago the Ring unfolded the world. It has not stopped. Last night the Pulse passed again, and the elder wants a word with you.
bestiary.truthLocked: Defeat one to learn what it really is.
bestiary.lore.slime: Seeps from small tears. It tastes of nothing, and that is the problem.
bestiary.lore.wolf: Ordinary wolves that live along the folds. They smell anchor stone and keep their distance.
bestiary.lore.scorpion: Desert creatures with shells a little harder than they should be. Blame a Pulse.
bestiary.lore.goblin: Kin of the Deep: small, clever, fond of warm iron. They talk, and they haggle. One once offered you a spoon to let it go.
bestiary.lore.archer: Not a ghost. A habit. The body repeats its last good shot.
bestiary.lore.boar: Driven from their old grounds by the drift. Nervous, and it shows.
bestiary.lore.golem: A shard of anchor stone that lost its wall. It walks toward the epicentre, like going home.
bestiary.lore.mage: People who lived too long by a tear. They learned to bend small folds. They can talk, if you let them.
bestiary.lore.troll: Flesh that grows in an extra direction: it heals fast and thinks slowly.
bestiary.lore.bat: Finds its way through the folds better than we do. Where we see nothing, it sees a door.
bestiary.lore.harpy: Its 'up' points slightly elsewhere. It falls upward along the folds.
bestiary.lore.wyvern: A big flyer that rides the folds. Its breath is warm with a dimension we can't see.
bestiary.lore.slime_king: The heart of the largest seep: slime that found a shape in itself.
bestiary.lore.alpha_wolf: Born by a tear. It remembers the wall and teaches the pack to go around it.
bestiary.lore.sand_tyrant: Something from the Deep surfaced in the dunes. To it, the desert is shallow water.
bestiary.lore.frost_giant: Stuck in a cold fold, slow and alone. Possibly thinking. Possibly sad.
bestiary.lore.bone_lord: The last night-duty officer of the Era of Ledgers. He lay in a fold so long he stopped dying.
bestiary.lore.ice_warden: The security system of a cryo lab. More polite than the people it guarded.
bestiary.lore.tomb_king: Head of the vault shift. He declared himself king. Nobody objected.
elder.title: Elder {name}
echo.undone: Somewhere near, a grave with your name on it is gone. The future it belonged to will not happen now. {name} saw to that, in a way.
grave.title: A grave
grave.future.title: A grave that should not be here yet
grave.hero: Here lies {hero} of {town}, who stood against {boss} in the year {year}. The wall held.
grave.future: Here lies the Wanderer of {town}. Fell to {boss} in the year {year}. Not yet.
chron.title: Chronicle
chron.empty: Nothing yet. Talk to elders, read graves, open chests: the past is lying around everywhere, and so is some of the future.
chron.founded: {founder} drove the first stake into the ground of {town}.
chron.wall.stone: The stone wall of {town} was finished. Every block of anchor stone was paid for twice.
chron.wall.palisade: {town} raised its fence. The priest blessed it; the carpenter sent the bill.
chron.pulse: The Pulse passed over {town}. Since then {fact}
chron.raid: {boss} came down on {town}. {hero} held the gate and did not come back.
chron.raid.other: In {teller} they tell it differently: when {boss} came down on {town}, {hero} ran, and the granary burned.
chron.raid.otherVersion: Others tell it differently: when {boss} came down on {town}, {hero} ran, and the granary burned.
chron.dungeon: Grandmothers say that when the world turned over, {facility} near {town} shut its doors with its keepers inside, and never opened them again. Now people call it the {theme}.
chron.valley: {walker} of {town} walked into a valley no road leads to in the year {year}, and walked out in the year {back}, the same afternoon.
chron.future: The Wanderer of {town} falls to {boss}. Unless.
chron.prophecy: They say a wanderer will fall to {boss} in the year {year}. There's already a grave. Go and look, if you like bad news.
chron.facility.5: the Feeding Hall (nobody knows why it had such strong doors)
chron.pulse.0: its well has given milk on feast days.
chron.pulse.1: everyone remembers two founders, and both are buried in the same grave.
chron.pulse.2: the river runs uphill on Sundays.
chron.pulse.3: its goats have spoken, though only about the weather.
chron.pulse.4: the town has always had a lighthouse. It is very far from the sea.
chron.pulse.5: the moon has been visible at noon, and nobody minds.
chron.pulse.6: the elder has been the same age for forty years.
chron.pulse.7: every map of the town shows one more street than there is.
chron.pulse.8: the bells ring a minute before anything happens.
chron.pulse.9: children are born remembering a song nobody taught them.
chron.pulse.10: the town has been at war with a neighbour that does not exist.
chron.pulse.11: its shadow has fallen the wrong way at dusk.
pulse.title: The world shifts
pulse.effect.strangers: Something is wrong with the land around you. It is still here, but it thinks it is {biome}, and the creatures believe it.
pulse.effect.surge: The air hums. Whatever lives around here has just been rewritten a little stronger.
pulse.effect.calm: Silence. The creatures around here are simply gone, as if they had never been written in.
pulse.effect.cache: A chest stands nearby that was not there a moment ago. In some other version of today, someone left it for you.
chron.pulse.live.strangers: The Pulse passed near {town}. For a while, creatures of the {biome} walked there.
chron.pulse.live.surge: The Pulse passed near {town}. For a while, every beast there was something worse.
chron.pulse.live.calm: The Pulse passed near {town}, and for a while there was not a single monster left to fight.
chron.pulse.live.cache: The Pulse passed near {town} and left a chest from another version of the day.
note.pulse.0: If found: return to me, yesterday. Reward offered.
note.pulse.1: You opened this before. You will open it again. Try the other hand this time.
note.pulse.2: Packed in a hurry, in a year that did not happen. Use well.
story.note.title: What you learned
story.m1.title: The Keystone Shard
story.m1.text: Take this: a shard of the stone our wall was cut from. {chronicler}, the chronicler in {town}, collects things that should not exist. Show it to them.
story.m1.done: {chronicler} turns the shard over and goes pale. "Anchor stone. Every wall we have is cut from it, and it is a piece of the Ring." They want the three calibration plates of the old world first. Then they will tell you what they know.
story.m1.chron: You brought a shard of wall stone to {chronicler} of {town}. Anchor stone is a piece of the Ring.
story.plate.crypt.title: The Plate of the Crypt
story.plate.crypt.text: The first plate lies in the {dungeon}, under whatever keeps it now. The night-duty logs say it was bolted to the wall of the control room.
story.plate.crypt.done: The plate is warm. Engraved: "CALIBRATION 1/3. DO NOT REMOVE WHILE RING IS LIVE." Someone scratched under it: "too late".
story.plate.crypt.chron: You took the first calibration plate from the {dungeon}.
story.plate.ice.title: The Plate of the Frozen Cave
story.plate.ice.text: The second plate was kept cold, they say, so that it would remember. Look in the {dungeon}.
story.plate.ice.done: Frost on the plate spells numbers that change when you look away. "CALIBRATION 2/3. FIELD STABLE. FIELD STABLE. FIELD STABLE."
story.plate.ice.chron: You took the second calibration plate from the {dungeon}.
story.plate.tomb.title: The Plate of the Sand Tomb
story.plate.tomb.text: The last plate is with the self-made king of the {dungeon}. He will not want to give it up. Nobody ever asked him nicely.
story.plate.tomb.done: Etched on the plate is a map: rings of lines around one point, far beyond the last town on any map. "CALIBRATION 3/3. RING IS THE ANCHOR."
story.plate.tomb.chron: You took the third calibration plate from the {dungeon}.
story.m5.title: Audience in {capital}
story.m5.text: All the plates you could find. Take them to {capital}. {ruler} keeps the old ledgers; with the plates they can finally be read. Go, before the next Pulse rewrites my nerve.
story.m5.done: {ruler} lays the plates on the ledgers, and the lines match. "The Shift was no accident that broke the Ring. The Ring works. It holds the fold open, and it cannot stop, because now it is what holds all of us up." The ledger names a place at the edge of the world.
story.m5.done.ended: {ruler} lays the plates on the ledgers, and the lines match. "The Shift was no accident that broke the Ring. The Ring did it." The ledger names a place at the edge of the world, a place you have already been.
story.m5.chron: In {capital}, {ruler} read the plates against the old ledgers: the Ring made the Shift. On its night-shift page, one face was not crossed out.
art.lore: Carried by {owner} of {town}, lost in the year {year}.
art.found.title: An artifact
art.found: {name}. {owner} of {town} lost it in the year {year}. The chronicles said it would be here, and for once they were right.
chron.artifact.dungeon: {owner} of {town} carried {artifact} down into the {theme} in the year {year}, and never came out.
chron.artifact.lair: {boss} swallowed {owner} of {town} in the year {year}, and {artifact} with them.
chron.artifact.valley: {owner} of {town} left {artifact} in a valley no road leads to, in the year {year}. On purpose, they said.
bestiary.lore.ring_keeper: The last safety system of the Ring. Three hundred years of keeping a door open has made it very sure the door must stay open.
ring.name: The Ring
ring.enter: Press E to go down to the Ring
ring.enter.touch: Tap Talk to go down to the Ring
story.m6.title: The Ring
story.m6.text: The ledger is clear: the Ring lies under the ground, about {far} tiles {dir} of {capital}, where nothing safe has stood for three hundred years. Go down. Then decide for all of us. I could not.
story.m6.done.fold: {ruler} listens without a word, then opens the window. No hum. "So this is quiet," they say. "We will have to learn to like it."
story.m6.done.open: {ruler} laughs, for the first time in years. "Then let it beat. We have lived inside a miracle for three centuries; we can stand a few more."
story.m6.chron: You went down to the Ring and came back to {capital} to tell {ruler} what you had chosen.
ending.title: The choice
ending.panel.title: The console of the Ring
ending.panel.text: One lever folds the dimension back. The Ring stops, the world sets into one version of itself, the hidden valleys go dark, and the stone that holds our walls goes cold. Leave it, and the Ring beats on: Pulses, echoes, all of it, forever. Nobody will be able to choose again.
ending.fold.name: Fold it back
ending.fold.desc: The Pulses stop. Echoes of the future fade, and the hidden valleys close. Anchor stone goes cold: the walls still stand, but they hold nothing back. One story, one past, and the tears stay where they are.
ending.open.name: Leave it open
ending.open.desc: The Ring beats on, faster now that nobody keeps it in check. More Pulses, richer and stranger. Everything born of the Shift lives on, and so does the danger.
ending.fold.note: You pull the lever. The hum you have heard all your life, without knowing it, stops. Somewhere above, a river decides to run downhill again. The world is one thing now. Go and tell them in the capital.
ending.open.note: You take your hand off the lever. The Ring hums on, louder, almost grateful. Above you the world is still unfinished, and it will stay that way. Go and tell them in the capital.
ending.fold.chron: At the console of the Ring you folded the dimension back. The Pulses stopped.
ending.open.chron: At the console of the Ring you left the dimension open. The Ring beats on.
elder.after.fold.0: No Pulse for weeks now. The goats have stopped talking. I miss them, a little.
elder.after.fold.1: The wall is cold to the touch now. Last night the wolves came right up to it and sniffed.
elder.after.fold.2: One past, one future. It is very restful. It is also a bit dull, between us.
elder.after.open.0: The Pulses come twice as often since you went down there. Business is good. Funerals too.
elder.after.open.1: Yesterday the bakery was a lighthouse. Today it is a bakery again, with a view.
elder.after.open.2: They say you could have stopped it. Thank you for not. Probably.
eq.head: Head
inv.hint.merchant: Right-click (or hold) an item in your backpack to sell it.
inv.hint.blacksmith: Select what to upgrade. Right-click (or hold) upgrades at once.
inv.tag.head: HEAD
say.priest.0: The Palm holds us, child. Mostly it holds us. Sit, if you need to.
say.priest.1: Every Pulse I rewrite the sermon. The flock never notices; I think the Pulse rewrites them too.
say.priest.2: The crypts below are old-world places. Whatever lies in them now does not pray.
say.innkeeper.0: Room, food, rumours. The first two cost money.
say.innkeeper.1: Travellers say the road east was shorter last week. Travellers say a lot of things.
say.innkeeper.2: If you are going anywhere, take a letter. Everybody here has someone out there.
say.captain.0: Walls hold. My people hold. The wilds do not care either way. Got a strong arm?
say.captain.1: Something big nests out there. I have the bounty, you have the legs.
say.captain.2: Keep inside the walls after dark. Or do not, and come back with ears. Paid by the pair.
say.chronicler.0: Every book here contradicts another book here. That is how I know the library is complete.
say.chronicler.1: Bring me something the old world left behind and I will tell you what it was. Probably.
say.chronicler.2: History is a list of things that happened, minus the Pulses. I keep both lists.
say.ruler.0: The crown is heavy, and it changes shape after every Pulse. Speak.
say.ruler.1: My ledgers say I have ruled for forty years. My mirror says nine. I believe the ledgers.
say.ruler.2: A kingdom is mostly walls, roads and people who argue. Thank you for the roads.
folk.say.0: Mind the well. It was a lighthouse on Tuesday.
folk.say.1: Have you seen my goat? It was talking a moment ago.
folk.say.2: The walls are anchor stone. Don't lick them, it doesn't help.
folk.say.3: Fresh bread! Mostly fresh. Fresh this version.
folk.say.4: My grandmother remembers the Shift. She's thirty.
folk.say.5: The road east was shorter yesterday, I swear.
folk.say.6: Elder's in the hall, if you're looking for trouble.
folk.say.7: The captain pays for ears. Don't ask whose.
folk.say.8: I dreamed the Pulse came and nothing changed. Worst dream I ever had.
folk.say.10: They say the Ring hums at night, if you put your ear to the ground.
folk.say.11: Two copper says you won't come back. Three says you will.
folk.say.12: Watch your purse. And your shadow, it's been odd lately.
folk.say.13: Lovely weather. Which weather is it today?
relic.relic_hard_hat.local: The crown of a very small, very practical king. Stops falling stones, they say.
relic.relic_hard_hat.truth: A hard hat. The Ring's crews wore it against falling tools. Yellow was for visibility, not for royalty.
relic.relic_hivis_vest.local: Robe of the Order of the Bright Stripe. It glows when a cart comes near.
relic.relic_hivis_vest.truth: A high-visibility vest. People wore it so that machines would notice them first.
relic.relic_wristwatch_back.local: Tells the time of yesterday. Popular with debtors.
relic.relic_wristwatch_back.truth: A wristwatch. The Pulse set it running backwards, and it has been counting down ever since.
relic.relic_lab_badge.local: Icon of the Patient Saint, who looks suspiciously like whoever holds it.
relic.relic_lab_badge.truth: An access badge of the Ring's night shift. The face on it is yours. The name has worn away.
relic.relic_safety_glasses.local: Spectacles for seeing what is not there. Prices vary; so does the not there.
relic.relic_safety_glasses.truth: Safety glasses, worn near sparks and acid so that the eyes would last longer than the job.
relic.relic_rubber_gloves.local: Skin of a patient swamp eel. Lightning slides off it.
relic.relic_rubber_gloves.truth: Insulating gloves, rated for high voltage. Rated; nobody has checked in three hundred years.
relic.relic_engineers_ring.local: A guild ring of the Iron Order. It tightens when you tell the truth.
relic.relic_engineers_ring.truth: An engineer's iron ring, worn as a reminder that bridges fall when promises do.
relic.relic_pointer_staff.local: A wand that points exactly where the speaker means. Never at the audience.
relic.relic_pointer_staff.truth: A telescopic pointer. People sat in rooms and watched pictures on a wall. It was called a meeting.
relic.relic_work_boots.local: Boots with an iron toe. Whoever wore them kicked doors for a living.
relic.relic_work_boots.truth: Steel-toe boots. The toe was for dropped wrenches, not for doors. The doors were an accident.
relic.relic_pipe_wrench.local: A heavy sword for people who do not trust swords. Also opens every pipe.
relic.relic_pipe_wrench.truth: A pipe wrench. It tightened pipes. That it is good at everything else is a coincidence.
relic.relic_coffee_mug.local: "World's Best Engineer." The Iron Order disputes the title.
relic.relic_coffee_mug.truth: A coffee mug with a joke on it. The joke was already old before the Shift.
relic.relic_lunchbox.local: A sealed iron chest of one small lunch. Opened once, by a fool, never again.
relic.relic_lunchbox.truth: A lunchbox. Somebody was hungry on the last night and never got to it. Do not open.
relic.relic_petri_dish.local: A glass saucer for blessing small things. Priests argue what the small things are.
relic.relic_petri_dish.truth: A petri dish, a lidded dish for growing tiny living things on jelly.
relic.relic_test_tube_rack.local: A tiny church organ with no pipes. It rattles when angry.
relic.relic_test_tube_rack.truth: A rack for test tubes. The tubes are gone; the rack still waits for them.
relic.relic_sample_jar.local: A jar of captured weather. Do not open on a Tuesday.
relic.relic_sample_jar.truth: A sealed sample jar. The label has a date on it, and the date is a long way back.
relic.relic_calculator.local: A pocket abacus with magic buttons. It only lies about sums.
relic.relic_calculator.truth: A calculator. People used it for arithmetic they could do themselves, only faster, and sometimes wrong.
relic.relic_stapler.local: A tiny iron dragon that bites paper. Keep it fed.
relic.relic_stapler.truth: A stapler. It joined pages with metal so that important papers were harder to lose. They were lost anyway.
relic.relic_rubber_duck.local: A yellow idol of the bath. Tell it your troubles; it never judges.
relic.relic_rubber_duck.truth: A rubber duck. Engineers explained their problems to it aloud, and the problem often solved itself.
relic.relic_kettle.local: A copper idol that sings when angry. Prophets say it has a second song.
relic.relic_kettle.truth: An electric kettle. Without power it is only a very patient jug.
relic.relic_fridge_magnet.local: A holy sigil that sticks to iron and to nothing else. Pilgrims collect them.
relic.relic_fridge_magnet.truth: A fridge magnet shaped like a seaside town. People pinned their holidays to the kitchen.
relic.relic_cookie_tin.local: A tin with cookies painted outside and sewing things inside. Both are lies.
relic.relic_cookie_tin.truth: A cookie tin. Everyone knew it held sewing thread. Everyone opened it hoping.
relic.relic_vending_coin.local: A coin of the Machine Kings. It buys only what the Machine remembers.
relic.relic_vending_coin.truth: A coin for a vending machine. The machine took it, thought about it, and sometimes gave out a snack.
relic.relic_ladle.local: A spoon the size of a helmet. Used in wars between pots.
relic.relic_ladle.truth: A kitchen ladle. Soup was the first thing anyone rebuilt after the Shift.
relic.relic_keycard.local: A thin white plate. Doors that remember it still open, sulking.
relic.relic_keycard.truth: An access card. It opened doors by being the right shape. Some doors still know it.
relic.relic_dead_phone.local: A black mirror that shows nothing. Some say the next Pulse. Nobody has the patience.
relic.relic_dead_phone.truth: A mobile phone, dead. Everyone carried one and looked at it all day. Now it looks back, blank.
relic.relic_hazard_sign.local: A warning of the Old Ones. The bolt means: run. It was right.
relic.relic_hazard_sign.truth: A high-voltage sign. The bolt meant: do not touch.
relic.relic_console_keycap.local: A square tooth from a giant's keyboard. Each one says a different letter.
relic.relic_console_keycap.truth: A keycap from the Ring's console. The letter has worn off. The Ring never needed it.
relic.relic_cold_sample.local: A jar of winter that never thaws. It keeps its keeper alive a little longer.
relic.relic_cold_sample.truth: A frozen sample from the cryo lab, kept cold by something that is not a machine any more.
relicset.night_shift.reward: The chronicler hands back your shift report, three hundred years late. Title: Night Operator.
relicset.lab.reward: What the cold kept, it gives back: the Cold Sample.
relicset.office.reward: "Middle Management." The chronicler is not sure it is an honour.
relicset.break_room.reward: Soup after the shift. The chronicler insists on paying for the kettle.
relicset.ring_works.reward: The chronicler marks on your map where the Ring is weakest from outside. Title: Maintenance.
relicset.chron.night_shift: You gathered your own desk from the old world, piece by piece: the Night Shift.
relicset.chron.lab: You gathered what the cryo lab left: the Lab.
relicset.chron.office: You gathered the office of the old world, rubber duck and all.
relicset.chron.break_room: You gathered the break room of the old world. The soup was the first thing rebuilt.
relicset.chron.ring_works: You gathered the tools of the Ring itself.
relic.unknown: Take it to a chronicler to learn what it really was.
relic.identified.more: The chronicler names {n} relics of the old world and pays {gold}g.
relic.found: A relic of the old world: {name}
relic.title: Relics of the old world
chronicler.badge: That face is yours. Do not look at me like that. I only read what is printed.
note.tomb.3: Held in trust: one badge, night operator. Went for coffee at 03:17. We kept the shift open.
console.roster.0: Roster check. Night shift: one operator missing for three hundred years. Welcome back.
console.roster.1: Coffee machine offline. Your desk has been collected. Almost all of it.
console.roster.2: Shift handover pending. Fold the dimension back, or leave it open? You have the floor.
relic.effect.ringCompass: Points the way to the Ring.
intro.0: Night shift, last hour. You went down for coffee. The stairs were longer than they should be.
intro.1: The Ring drew a breath, and the world folded around you like a page.
intro.2: One lunch later you step out of the fold. The gate is stone, the guard is old, and three hundred years are gone.
intro.3: You remember very little: a stairwell, a hum, a taste of coffee. The Ring still hums. Somebody should finish the shift.
elder.first.0: You came out of the gate-fold at dawn. Last time it was goats. You look better than the goats.
elder.first.1: That coat is older than my wall. Old-world cloth does not rot. It waits for someone who knows what it is.
elder.first.2: No name? Then you are the Wanderer until you remember. The post is vacant. Wells first.
intro.title: The night shift
relic.empty: Nothing yet. Things of the old world turn up in chests, with bosses, in hidden valleys and in Pulse caches. A chronicler in a city can tell you what they were.
dlg.fallback.done: You did it. Here, as promised.

deed.q_gate_3.keep.tale: The captain says the Wanderer spoke for that goat, so she sleeps inside the wall now. Nobody asked me. She eats my notices.
deed.q_gate_3.keep.chron: The Wanderer of {town} spoke for a goat that came out of the fold, and the goat stayed inside the wall.
deed.q_gate_3.free.tale: In the market they say the Wanderer sent a goat back into the fold. She went to the last field. Hesk wept, though. He says it was the wind.
deed.q_gate_3.free.chron: The Wanderer of {town} let a goat from the fold go free. Old Hesk walked her out to the last field.
folk.deed.q_gate_3.keep.0: The goat by the gate is called Wanderer. Don't take it personally.
folk.deed.q_gate_3.keep.1: That goat ate my hat. The elder says she's a bad sign. She's a bad goat.
folk.deed.q_gate_3.keep.2: Old Hesk sleeps in a goat pen now. Happiest I've seen him.
folk.deed.q_gate_3.free.0: There's a goat in the last field. Don't feed her. Hesk does that.
folk.deed.q_gate_3.free.1: Wolves keep off the last field. There's a goat. Think what you like.
folk.deed.q_gate_3.free.2: Hesk talks to the last field every morning. Only the goat answers.
deed.q_eel_3.hide.tale: They say the Wanderer looked down the north well and saw nothing. The priest says so too. They say it the same way, which is odd.
deed.q_eel_3.hide.chron: At the north well of {town} the Wanderer saw nothing at all, and said so to the priest.
deed.q_eel_3.tell.tale: They say the Wanderer found the holy eel at the bottom of the north well, guarding a treasure. There was no treasure. There is a queue.
deed.q_eel_3.tell.chron: The Wanderer told the priest of {town} what was in the north well. The pilgrims went there, and the church went quiet.
folk.deed.q_eel_3.hide.0: Empty bowl at the church. Still the best sermon in town.
folk.deed.q_eel_3.hide.1: Somebody leaves bread at the north well. Not me. Not the priest, either.
folk.deed.q_eel_3.hide.2: The priest blesses the north well twice now. Says it needs it.
folk.deed.q_eel_3.tell.0: Can't get to the well for pilgrims. I've started drinking ale. For safety.
folk.deed.q_eel_3.tell.1: The eel's in the north well. Don't drink it. Don't drink near it.
folk.deed.q_eel_3.tell.2: The church is half empty. The priest looks ten years younger.
deed.q_cellar_2.seal.tale: They say the Wanderer had the innkeeper wall up a door to nowhere. My ledger has a new line now: the inn. The wall is delighted.
deed.q_cellar_2.seal.chron: On the Wanderer's word, the innkeeper of {town} walled up the tear in his cellar with anchor stone, and paid for it.
deed.q_cellar_2.sell.tale: They say the Wanderer showed our innkeeper how to sell a hole in the ground. He did not need much showing.
deed.q_cellar_2.sell.chron: On the Wanderer's word, the innkeeper of {town} kept the tear in his cellar open, and began to sell tickets.
folk.deed.q_cellar_2.seal.0: The inn walled up its cellar. Beer's dearer. Sleep's cheaper.
folk.deed.q_cellar_2.seal.1: Something knocks under the inn on Sundays. The innkeeper knocks back.
folk.deed.q_cellar_2.seal.2: The inn owes the wall now. The wall never forgets a debt.
folk.deed.q_cellar_2.sell.0: One copper to see the crack. I paid three. Worth it.
folk.deed.q_cellar_2.sell.1: My uncle put his arm in the crack. Now he waves at us from further away.
folk.deed.q_cellar_2.sell.2: The queue for the cellar is longer than the queue for church.
quest.q_cellar_3b.title: Paid in Grey
quest.q_ysa.title: Two Moons Late
quest.q_book.title: Someone Who Reads
item.marra_book.found: Behind Pell's counter, under a sack of onions: a smoke-dark book, and eleven jars.
item.marra_book.name: Marra's Book
item.marra_book.desc: Hand-sewn, smoke-dark. Small square writing about hinges and heats. The last page has one line: 'Hammer's under Ysa's step. Leave it.'
quest.q_letter.title: In Writing
item.brannoc_letter.name: Brannoc's Letter
item.brannoc_letter.desc: Folded twice, sealed with a sooty thumb. Two lines, by the feel of it. The second pressed harder.
item.marra_hammer.found: Under the bottom step, wrapped in sacking: a smith's hammer. Off in the trees, the wolves start up.
item.marra_hammer.name: Marra's Hammer
item.marra_hammer.desc: A smith's hammer, the handle black with use. A wedge of grey stone is set through the head. It is warm.
quest.q_hammer_b.title: With the Forge
quest.q_hammer_k.title: Here, Not There
quest.q_herbs.title: Winter Salve
item.slowleaf.name: Slowleaf
item.slowleaf.desc: Picked an hour ago, or a week. You can't tell by looking.
say.pell.0: Everything fairly priced. Fair to me, anyway.
say.pell.1: Salve? I've a few jars. Very few. Very dear.
say.pell.2: Cash, credit or a favour. I like favours. They keep.
say.brannoc.0: Borrowed hammer. Works. Doesn't ring. Buy something or sit down.
say.brannoc.1: I hung the town gate with my gran when I was twelve. Still swings. Don't lean on it.
say.brannoc.2: If Kell sent you, the door's behind you.
say.kell.0: WELCOME! Mind the anvil. Mind the sparks. Mind ME, I'm working!
say.kell.1: My cousin's a smith too. A sort of a smith. Up the road. Don't buy from him.
say.kell.2: Borrowed hammer. Like hitting iron with a loaf.
say.ysa.0: Kettle's on. Sit if you like. Mind the green pot; it bites.
say.ysa.1: A house, a step and me. The wolves have been polite lately. Lucky.
say.ysa.2: Pell sends his regards, I expect. Never his money.
deed.q_hammer_b.done.tale: They say Marra's hammer turned up under the herb-woman's step. Brannoc has it now. The wolves have the step.
deed.q_hammer_b.done.chron: Marra's hammer was found under a step in the wood and went home to her forge.
folk.deed.q_hammer_b.done.0: Brannoc's forge rings again. Like old Marra's.
folk.deed.q_hammer_b.done.1: Brannoc smiled at a horse yesterday. The horse bolted.
folk.deed.q_hammer_b.done.2: Wolves at the herb-woman's door now, they say. Never used to be.
deed.q_hammer_k.done.tale: They say Brannoc sent for Marra's hammer, and Kell's forge rings with it. Ask the Wanderer how. Brannoc has.
deed.q_hammer_k.done.chron: Sent for Marra's hammer by Brannoc, the Wanderer carried it to Kell instead.
folk.deed.q_hammer_k.done.0: Kell's forge rings like old Marra's. Brannoc's doesn't. Funny, that.
folk.deed.q_hammer_k.done.1: Brannoc sent for a hammer, they say. Kell paid for it.
folk.deed.q_hammer_k.done.2: The herb-woman's lost her luck, they say. Wolves on her step.
quest.q_hammer_b.goal: Find Marra's hammer at Ysa's farm
quest.q_hammer_k.goal: Find Marra's hammer at Ysa's farm
quest.q_ysa.goal: Find Ysa, out in the glade
